title: Does Jasmine Tea Have Caffeine? (Yes — From Its Tea Base)
meta_description: Yes — jasmine tea has caffeine from its tea base (usually green, ~30–50 mg/cup), not the jasmine flowers. Published figures and why the base tea matters.

body_html:
Yes — jasmine tea has caffeine, and it comes entirely from the tea leaves, not the jasmine blossoms. Most jasmine tea is green tea scented with jasmine flowers, which puts a typical 8 oz cup around 30–50 mg, in line with green tea generally. Healthline reports a wider published range of 15–60 mg per cup, noting the number depends on which base tea was used. Jasmine-scented black or white tea exists too, and shifts the number up or down accordingly.

How much caffeine is in jasmine tea?

Per Healthline, jasmine tea “contains 15–60 mg of caffeine per cup (237 ml) — depending on how long the tea leaves steep and which type of tea is used as a base.” That's a wide range because “jasmine tea” isn't one fixed tea — it's a scenting process applied to a base tea, and the base tea is what actually determines the caffeine.

What is jasmine tea, really?

Jasmine tea is a flavored true tea, not an herbal tisane — a common mix-up, since it's named after a flower and often shelved near genuinely caffeine-free floral teas like chamomile or hibiscus. Healthline describes the process directly: it's “typically based on green tea, but sometimes black or white tea is used instead,” and “blossoms from common jasmine (Jasminum officinale) or sampaguita (Jasminum sambac) are placed alongside tea leaves in storage or blended with stored tea, allowing the aroma to infuse.” The flowers perfume the leaves; they don't contribute any caffeine of their own. For the full true-tea-vs-tisane distinction, see our what is a tisane guide.

Why the base tea is what matters

Because jasmine tea is a scented version of an existing tea, its caffeine tracks whichever base was used:

  • Jasmine green tea (the most common version) — tracks green tea's typical 30–50 mg per 8 oz cup, averaging around 35 mg on this site's canonical figures.
  • Jasmine white tea — tracks white tea's lower typical range, about 15–30 mg per 8 oz cup.
  • Jasmine black tea — a less common but real variant — tracks black tea's higher typical range, about 40–70 mg per 8 oz cup.

A package labeled simply “jasmine tea” with no base specified is most often the green-tea version, which is why the general published range (Healthline's 15–60 mg) centers closer to green tea's own figures than to black tea's.

Jasmine tea vs. green tea vs. other teas, compared

Use the calculator above to compare jasmine's most common (green-tea) base against any other drink, by the cup or across a full day, or check the static reference table below:

DrinkServingTypical caffeineRange
Jasmine tea (published range, Healthline)8 oz—15–60 mg
White tea (steeped)8 oz~25 mg15–30 mg
Green tea (steeped — jasmine's usual base)8 oz~35 mg30–50 mg
Black tea (steeped — some jasmine blends)8 oz~50 mg40–70 mg
Matcha1 tsp (2 g) whisked in 2–3 oz~65–70 mg60–80 mg
Espresso1 oz shot~63 mg60–80 mg
Brewed coffee8 oz~95 mg80–100 mg
Rooibos / herbal (caffeine-free)8 oz0 mgcaffeine-free

The takeaway: a jasmine green tea and a plain green tea occupy essentially the same caffeine range, because they're the same leaf — one just carries a floral scent. Only when the base changes (to black or white tea) does jasmine tea's caffeine meaningfully move.

Is jasmine tea an herbal tea?

No — this is the most common misconception about it. Jasmine tea is frequently confused with true herbal tisanes (chamomile, hibiscus, peppermint) because of the flower in its name and its floral, fragrant character. But those tisanes are infusions of plants that never produced caffeine to begin with, while jasmine tea is scented Camellia sinensis — the actual tea plant — and carries real caffeine from that leaf. See our herbal tea caffeine guide for the full list of genuinely caffeine-free options.

Is jasmine tea's caffeine a lot?

At roughly 15–60 mg per cup (with a typical jasmine-green cup closer to 30–50 mg), jasmine tea is a modest share of the general daily reference the U.S. FDA has cited — about 400 mg per day as a level not generally associated with negative effects for most healthy adults. That reference covers everything caffeinated you drink in a day, not any single cup. People who are pregnant, caffeine-sensitive, or managing a health condition should talk to a healthcare provider about what caffeine level is appropriate for them.

For how jasmine's usual green-tea base compares on its own, see green tea caffeine. For the complete true-tea-vs-tisane breakdown, see what is a tisane.

This describes published research and general information, not medical or dietary advice.

faqs.a: Yes. Most jasmine tea is green tea scented with jasmine flowers, so it carries green tea's caffeine — typically 30–50 mg per 8 oz cup. Healthline reports a wider published range of 15–60 mg, since the exact base tea and steep time both matter.

faqs.q: How much caffeine is in jasmine tea?
faqs.a: Healthline reports 15–60 mg per 8 oz cup, depending on the base tea and steep time. Jasmine green tea, the most common version, typically lands around 30–50 mg.
No. Jasmine tea is a scented true tea, not a caffeine-free herbal tisane. Its caffeine comes from the base tea leaf (usually green), not the jasmine flowers, which contribute aroma only.

faqs.q: Is jasmine tea an herbal tea?
faqs.a: No — this is a common mix-up because of the flower in its name. Jasmine tea is scented Camellia sinensis (real tea leaf), not an infusion of a naturally caffeine-free plant like chamomile or hibiscus.

faqs.q: Is jasmine tea the same as jasmine green tea?
faqs.a: Usually, yes — most jasmine tea sold is jasmine-scented green tea, the most common base. But jasmine-scented white or black tea also exist and carry different caffeine ranges.

faqs.q: Does jasmine tea have as much caffeine as green tea?
faqs.a: Jasmine green tea specifically does — it's the same green tea leaf with jasmine scenting added, so it tracks green tea's typical 30–50 mg per 8 oz cup.

faqs.q: Does jasmine tea have more caffeine than black tea?
faqs.a: Not usually. Most jasmine tea uses a green tea base (30–50 mg per cup), which runs below black tea's typical range (40–70 mg). Jasmine black tea, a less common variant, would track black tea's higher range instead.

faqs.q: Do the jasmine flowers add caffeine to the tea?
faqs.a: No. Jasmine blossoms are layered with the tea leaves purely to transfer their scent; they don't contain caffeine and don't change the base tea's caffeine content.

faqs.q: Is jasmine pearl tea more caffeinated than regular jasmine tea?
faqs.a: Jasmine pearls are hand-rolled jasmine green tea, so they carry the same green-tea-based caffeine range as other jasmine green teas — roughly 30–50 mg per 8 oz cup. Rolling and grading don't reliably change the caffeine figure.

faqs.q: Does jasmine tea have more caffeine than coffee?
faqs.a: No. Even at the high end of Healthline's published range (60 mg), jasmine tea stays well below brewed coffee's typical 80–100 mg per 8 oz cup.

faqs.q: Can I drink jasmine tea if I'm avoiding caffeine?
faqs.a: Not if you need a true 0 mg option — jasmine tea has real caffeine from its tea base. For a genuinely caffeine-free floral option, look for rooibos or hibiscus, which are herbal tisanes, not scented true tea.
